$comment: RIFTBORN ammunition. Lethal rounds go in chamber A, capture rounds in chamber B.

capture.name: Heavy Sedative Dart
capture.note: Slow projectile with heavy drop. Leads moving targets badly.

capture.name: Anchor Tether
capture.note: Mandatory for any Colossus or Titan capture.

formulas.damage: base_damage * ammo_damage_multiplier * element_multiplier * hit_zone_damage * (1 - armour_reduction) * ambush_multiplier
formulas.restraint_gain: weapon_base_restraint * ammo_restraint_multiplier * element_multiplier * hit_zone_restraint * status_product * wound_multiplier * ambush_multiplier / size_resistance
formulas.restraint_decay_per_second: (4.0 + 0.35 * species_tier) * status_decay_multiplier * lerp(at_zero_hp, at_full_hp, current_hp / max_hp)
formulas.weak_point_damage_note: A weak point hit uses the weapon's crit_multiplier in place of hit_zones.weak_point.damage; the hit_zones value is the default for weapons that do not define one.
formulas.restraint_decay_note: Statuses scale decay: a status with halts_restraint_decay stops it entirely, otherwise decay_multiplier values multiply together.
formulas.flee_speed: species_speed * (0.75 + 0.6 * current_hp / max_hp) -- a badly wounded monster limps, so a chase is winnable rather than a formality

$restraint_required_scale_note: Converts between two independently authored ladders: weapon `restraint` (14-58 per projectile) and species `base_restraint` (22-1100). Without it a sedated weak-point dart on a wounded Strider fills the whole bar in one shot. Raise it to make every capture slower; it is the single global dial for capture pacing.
$flee_chance_scale_note: Global multiplier on every species' skittishness, kept at 1.0 so the bestiary's published values stand. It exists because the flee rate was losing roughly a quarter of straightforward culls; that turned out to be better fixed by making a badly wounded monster limp (see formulas.flee_speed) than by blunting the flee roll, which would have removed the drama instead of giving the player an answer to it.
$restraint_decay_health_scale_note: A healthy monster shakes off sedative faster than a wounded one. This is what stops 'swap to darts at half health' being a strategy with no failure mode: dart it early and the meter drains against you.
$wound_multiplier_exponent_note: Curves the wound multiplier instead of ramping it linearly. Linear left almost no gradient between 50% and 30% health (2.0 vs 2.4), so darting early cost the same per capture as wounding deeply first and never risked the flee threshold — it strictly dominated. Curving it makes the timing of the chamber swap the decision it is supposed to be.
$field_comment:
Field items are the only thing you can do about a wounded party WITHOUT going home. Health and PP carry across a patrol, which makes a patrol about three fights long; without a field item the only answers are walk back to the Sanctuary or wait out the regen clock, and 'wait half an hour' is not a thing you can ask of someone standing in a street.

Using one IN BATTLE costs the turn, and that turn is the whole balance. Measured (FIELD=1 in balance_sim.mjs): a salve restoring 40% is worth +15 points of win rate and the DUMBEST policy scores best — heal whenever you are low beats reading the matchup, so it is a button you hold, and it cancels the patrol limit this whole system exists to create. At 18% — about one turn of incoming damage, which is what the comparable-damage cap holds an exchange to — healing is worth only +3 flat, and a policy that reads whether the damage race is close beats every flat rule while spending FEWER salves. That is a decision, so that is what in_battle items are tuned to.

The generous restores are therefore NOT usable in a fight. They work between battles, on patrol, where extending the patrol is exactly their job and they cannot make a losing fight winnable by attrition.

field.name: Field Salve
field.note: About one turn of incoming damage. Deliberately marginal: worth the turn when the race is close, wasted when it is not.

field.name: Focus Draught
field.note: 4 PP back on every move. Costs the turn, so it only pays when the alternative is several turns of Strike.

field.name: Deep Salve
field.note: Most of the bar, between fights only. In a fight this was worth +15 points and made healing a button you hold.

field.name: Rouse Vial
field.note: Brings one back from down, at half. The only way to un-lose a monster mid-patrol, and never mid-fight.

field_drops.$comment:
Field items are craftable at the bench, and until now that was the ONLY way to get one: nothing in the world handed you a salve for playing. A kit you can only buy is a kit most players never carry, which makes the whole field-item system something you read about rather than use.

Two constraints decided these numbers rather than taste.

First, drops must not cancel the patrol limit. FIELD=1 measured that a generous heal is worth +15 points of win rate and makes the dumbest policy the best one; PATROL=1 measured that a full kit buys about one extra battle. A drop rate that refills the kit faster than a patrol spends it turns 'go home and mend' into 'keep walking', which is the one thing the condition system exists to prevent. Measured, the patrol limit turned out NOT to be the binding constraint: at five times these rates a patrol still runs 2.0 battles against 1.9 with nothing, because drops arrive at the rate the patrol ends and a patrol is only about two battles long. What drops really change is the economy between patrols, so the rate is set against that instead — about one kit's worth (four items) per evolution milestone, which PROGRESS=1 puts at 7.4 patrols. The world supplies roughly one kit per milestone and the bench supplies the rest.

Second, culling and cataloguing drop at the SAME rate. The design has always held that both paths are legitimate — culling pays today, cataloguing pays in three weeks — and a loot table that favours one would quietly settle that argument in a way no document agreed to.
field_drops.$weights_note: Which item, once something drops. Deep Salve is the one that extends a patrol, so it is deliberately the scarce one; Rouse Vial un-loses a monster and is scarcer still.
